strategy_roster.name: Chandelier Exit with 200 EMA Filter
strategy_roster.notes: The Chandelier long level is the 22-bar high minus three ATR(22) and the documented 200 EMA filter is kept; the same level acts as the trailing exit. Only the EMA length is documented (200 in the name), so the 22/3 ATR settings are standard Chandelier fallbacks, and the close-versus-extremum option is not expressible.

strategy_roster.name: RAVI + Awesome Oscillator
strategy_roster.notes: RAVI is approximated by a fast versus slow EMA spread and the Awesome Oscillator by the documented 5/34 median-price spread, so both must be bullish. FastLength/SlowLength have no documented values, so 7/30 are fallbacks, and the pip stop, target and trailing distances are not percentage fields.

strategy_roster.name: 4218 RSI MA
strategy_roster.notes: The RSI_MA oscillator is approximated by RSI(14) as the activation test plus the slope of EMA(14) on the documented weighted price (High+Low+2*Close)/4. The oversold/overbought extreme and activation levels, pip stops and risk-percent sizing are name-only parameters and are not encoded.

strategy_roster.name: Ha MaZi
strategy_roster.entry_long: low <= donchian_low_prev(low,13) and close > open and close > ema(close,40)
strategy_roster.notes: ZigzagLength=13 new pivots are approximated by the prior 13-bar extreme, the bullish Heikin Ashi candle by a positive candle with close above its open, and MaPeriod=40 is kept as the EMA filter. StopLoss 70 and TakeProfit 200 are fixed point distances, not percentages, and ZigZag/Heikin Ashi internals are not available.

strategy_roster.name: T3MA(MTC)
strategy_roster.notes: The documented double-smoothed EMA with MaPeriod=4 is written literally and the signal is a flip of its slope, which matches the T3MA-ALARM rising/falling change. MaShift, the CalculationBarOffset signal queue and StartProtection in price steps (40/11) are not expressible.

strategy_roster.name: Backbone Basket Strategy (StockSharp)
strategy_roster.notes: It seeds a direction from bid/ask extremes and then keeps adding one market order per candle until MaxTrades=10, alternating long and short baskets with fractional risk sizing, so it is a multi-order accumulation engine. The never-true guard is used rather than inventing a single-bar signal; point stops are not percentages.

strategy_roster.name: HSV and HSL Gradient Tools
strategy_roster.notes: The docs list RGB/HSV/HSL conversion, gradient and easing helpers and state trade logic: none. With no market-derived signal the never-true guard is used.

strategy_roster.name: Divergence For Many Indicators
strategy_roster.entry_long: low < donchian_low_prev(low,10) and roc(rsi(close,14),5) > 0 and roc(macd(close,12,26),5) > 0
strategy_roster.notes: A bullish divergence is written as a new 10-bar low while both documented oscillators (RSI 14, MACD 12/26) have rising 5-bar momentum, i.e. at least MinDivergence=2 confirmations. The docs give no values for the periods, MinDivergence or the divergence lookback, so 14/12/26/10 are fallbacks, and the exit is an explicit reversal proxy.

strategy_roster.name: Friday Bond Short
strategy_roster.notes: A time-based, short-only schedule that sells Friday 13:00 ET and buys back Monday 13:00 ET using no indicators. The DSL has no day-of-week or hour field, so the never-true guard is used rather than faking a market signal.

strategy_roster.name: RSI Cyclic Smoothed
strategy_roster.notes: DominantCycleLength=20 is used for the oscillator and its dynamic percentile bands are approximated by Bollinger bands of the RSI series, entering on the documented lower-band cross and exiting on the upper-band cross. Vibration=10 and Leveling=10 have no documented mapping and the stops have no values, so both are null.
